policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'straightway in the morning' renders either adverb (euthys/eutheos) and the extra preposition phrase leaves no English trace; nothing in the verse or its notes distinguishes them.
The added article before Pilate is invisible in English: ASV 'delivered him up to Pilate' is identical under either reading.
ASV 'And he answering saith unto him' uses the present 'saith', rendering legei; the aorist eipen would give 'said'.
ASV 'Pilate again asked him' renders imperfect or aorist alike; the English past tense does not distinguish epērōta from epērōtēsen.
ASV 'how many things they accuse thee of' renders katēgorousin (accuse); katamartyrousin would give 'witness against'.
ASV 'whom they asked of him' fits either the compound relative with ēitounto or hon parēitounto; the only note here is an alternative_rendering about 'a feast' and cannot decide a reading.
ASV 'them that had made insurrection' renders stasiastōn or the sy- compound alike; the English marks no 'fellow' element that would isolate systasiastōn.
ASV 'the multitude went up' renders anabas; anaboēsas would give 'crying out'/'cried aloud'.
ASV 'as he was wont to do unto them' expresses the habitual force of the imperfect and does not require the added aei; no note maps here.
ASV 'again answered and said' preserves neither the Greek word order nor the imperfect/aorist difference between elegen and eipen.
ASV 'What then shall I do unto him' has no rendering of thelete; the reading with thelete requires 'what will ye then that I do', as in KJV.
ASV 'him whom ye call the King of the Jews' renders hon legete explicitly; the omission leaves no clause for those words.
Presence or absence of the article before 'King' is not marked by ASV's 'the King of the Jews', which supplies the English article either way.
Word order only; ASV 'what evil hath he done' is fixed by English syntax under either arrangement.
ASV 'cried out exceedingly' renders the positive perissōs; the comparative perissoterōs is rendered 'the more exceedingly' (so KJV here).
Both endidyskousin and endyousin are 'they clothe him'; ASV's wording does not distinguish the synonyms.
ASV 'Hail, King of the Jews!' renders the vocative and the nominative-for-vocative identically.
ASV 'put on him his garments' renders the plain possessive autou; ta idia would give 'his own garments', which ASV elsewhere marks with 'own'.
Aorist subjunctive versus future indicative after hina; ASV's purpose clause 'to crucify him' does not distinguish them.
The article before the place name leaves no trace in ASV 'unto the place Golgotha'.
Declensional spelling of the name only; ASV transliterates 'Golgotha' under either form.
Neuter or masculine participle agreement is invisible in ASV 'which is, being interpreted'.
ASV 'they offered him wine mingled with myrrh' has no rendering of the added piein; that reading yields 'gave him to drink wine' (so KJV).
Relative hos or article ho as subject; ASV 'but he received it not' renders either.
ASV 'And they crucify him, and part his garments' has a finite present 'crucify' joined by 'and'; the aorist participle staurōsantes would give 'and when they had crucified him'.
The ASV text prints no verse 28; the sentence about the scripture being fulfilled appears only in a margin ('Many ancient authorities insert verse 28'), so the text follows the shorter reading.
ASV 'buildest it in three days' renders the dative with or without en, and English word order is fixed regardless; the notes here concern verse 28 and the rendering 'sanctuary'.
ASV 'save thyself, and come down from the cross' coordinates a second imperative, rendering kai kataba; the participle katabas would give 'save thyself, coming down from the cross'.
The added article before Israel is not marked in ASV 'the King of Israel'.
ASV 'that we may see and believe' supplies no object; the reading with autō requires 'believe him'.
ASV 'they that were crucified with him' renders the compound verb with or without the redundant syn.
ASV opens 'And when the sixth hour was come', rendering the connective kai; the postpositive de reading gives 'Now/But when...'.
Word order and the article with the hour leave ASV 'at the ninth hour' unchanged.
ASV 'cried with a loud voice, Eloi, Eloi' has no 'saying'; ASV renders legōn where it stands, so the added participle is absent from its text.
ASV transliterates 'lama sabachthani', matching lama; lema and lima would give 'lema'/'lima'.
Word order only; ASV 'why hast thou forsaken me' is fixed by English syntax under either arrangement.
ASV 'Behold, he calleth Elijah' renders ide and idou alike.
ASV 'And one ran, and filling a sponge' coordinates the two participles with 'and', which requires the kai of r00-base/r02 and excludes r01; but 'one' renders tis and heis alike.
The connective te leaves no trace in ASV 'put it on a reed, and gave him to drink'.
The ASV text reads 'saw that he so gave up the ghost' and its textual_variant note assigns 'so cried out, and gave up the ghost' to 'many ancient authorities', so the text lacks kraxas.
Word order only; ASV 'this man' is the same under either arrangement.
Word order only; ASV 'was the Son of God' does not reflect the position of the copula.
English requires a verb regardless: ASV 'among whom were both Mary Magdalene...' supplies 'were' whether or not ēn stands in the Greek.
ASV writes 'Mary' for both Maria and Mariam.
The extra article in 'James the less' is invisible in ASV's English.
ASV writes 'Joses' for either genitive form Iōsētos or Iōsē.
ASV 'who, when he was in Galilee, followed him' has no 'also'; ASV renders adverbial kai as 'also' (cf. 'who also himself was looking', v. 43), so the added kai is absent.
ASV 'the day before the sabbath' renders the compound noun and the prepositional phrase alike.

ASV gives two coordinate finite verbs, 'there came Joseph... ; and he boldly went in unto Pilate', rendering ēlthen; ASV preserves circumstantial participles as participles in this context (v. 46 'taking him down, wound him').
The article with the place phrase leaves 'Joseph of Arimathaea' unchanged in English.
The article before the proper name is not marked in ASV 'went in unto Pilate'.
ASV's second clause reads 'whether he had been any while dead', rendering palai; its textual_variant note assigns 'were already dead' (ēdē) to other authorities, so the text has palai.
ASV 'he granted the corpse to Joseph' renders ptōma; sōma would give 'the body'.
English coordination is required either way: ASV 'he bought a linen cloth, and taking him down' would read the same without the Greek kai.
ASV 'laid him in a tomb' renders ethēken and the compound katethēken alike.
ASV writes 'tomb' for both mnēmeiō and mnēmati.
ASV 'Mary the mother of Joses' supplies the relationship in either case; the article and the genitive spelling leave no English trace.
After the past main verb 'beheld', ASV 'where he was laid' renders the perfect tetheitai and the present tithetai in secondary sequence alike.
